primitives.name: Short Rest Variance Effect
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Observation - Teams on short rest tend to show higher result variance than teams on standard rest in the samples reviewed.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V_{\\text{rest}}': 'dimensionless variance measure', 't_{\\text{gap}}': 'time gap between games in days'}
primitives.assumptions: Variance increases monotonically with t_gap < 3 days, independent of sport type.

layer2.mapping: Stochastic perturbation kernel applied to baseline score distribution, increasing volatility parameter σ².
layer2.telemetry: Observed margin variance relative to standard rest sample

primitives.name: Travel Uncertainty Factor
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Long cross-country travel before an early local kickoff is frequently cited; in the data reviewed the effect is small and noisy once injuries and opponent strength are accounted for.
primitives.assumptions: U_travel scales logarithmically with d_dist, with diminishing returns beyond 1000km.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to fatigue propagation model in biomechanical systems, where U_travel acts as a damping factor.
layer2.telemetry: Post-travel performance deviation from expected baseline

primitives.name: Confounding Noise Dominance
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Confounds dominate: injury status, roster-rest decisions, and opponent quality can each be larger than the rest/travel signal itself.
primitives.assumptions: N_confound ≥ max(V_rest, U_travel), with additive noise structure.

layer2.mapping: Noise kernel dominates signal kernel in likelihood function, reducing signal-to-noise ratio.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of observed variance to predicted variance under control conditions

The primitives define a hierarchical uncertainty model where short rest introduces variance (V_rest), travel adds noise (U_travel), and confounding variables dominate signal detection (N_confound). These interact through a multiplicative noise framework, where V_rest and U_travel act as variance multipliers, while N_confound acts as a stochastic suppression term. The system exhibits non-linear sensitivity to t_gap and d_dist, with regime boundaries at t_gap ≤ 2 and d_dist > 1000 km. The epistemic failure mode arises when confounding is not controlled, leading to spurious correlation claims. Dualities emerge in that variance increase due to rest is mirrored by uncertainty increase due to travel, but both are attenuated by confounding. The model's robustness depends on sample size correction and multi-season pooling, which introduces additional heterogeneity.
